title.zh: 卷466 列傳二百五十三 徐用仪 许景澄 袁昶 立山 联元
title.en: Volume 466 Biographies 253: Xu Yongyi, Xu Jingcheng, Yuan Chang, Li Shan, Lian Yuan
title.raw: 卷466 列傳二百五十三 徐用仪 许景澄 袁昶 立山 联元

sentences.zh: 徐用儀，字筱雲，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Xu Yongyi, courtesy name Xiaoyun, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yongyi, whose courtesy name was Xiaoyun, came from Haiyan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 由副貢生入貲為主事，官刑部。

translations.literal: Through the office purchased by deputy tribute graduates he became a principal secretary and served in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Having bought office as a deputy tribute graduate, he entered service as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年，舉順天鄉試．同治初，充軍機章京，兼直總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he passed the metropolitan examination in Shuntian; at the beginning of the Tongzhi reign he served as a Grand Council clerk and concurrently attended the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 9 he passed the Shuntian provincial examination; early in Tongzhi he became a Grand Council clerk and also served at the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 累遷鴻臚寺少卿，以憂歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and returned home on bereavement leave.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then left office to mourn a parent.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，起太僕寺少卿，遷大理寺卿，直軍機如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and transferred to President of the Court of Judicial Review, continuing to attend the Grand Council as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3 he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then made President of the Court of Judicial Review while still attending the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 擢工部侍郎，始罷直。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and only then ceased regular attendance at the Council.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of Works, he at last gave up his regular seat on the Council.

sentences.zh: 旋充總理衙門大臣，歷兵部、吏部侍郎，授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he served as a Zongli Yamen minister, passed through the vice ministries of War and Personnel, and was appointed a Grand Council minister.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a Zongli Yamen minister, served as vice minister of War and of Personnel in turn, and was appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 of the reign he received the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 日朝搆为，舉朝爭議和戰，樞臣孫毓汶被劾罷，翁同龢繼入，主戰益力。

translations.literal: Japan stirred up trouble; the whole court debated peace and war; Grand Councillor Sun Yuwen was impeached and dismissed; Weng Tonghe succeeded him and pressed for war all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan provoked conflict, the court split over peace and war; Grand Councillor Sun Yuwen was impeached out of office, and Weng Tonghe took his place and argued for war even harder.

sentences.zh: 用儀論事與同龢忤，遂出樞廷，並解總署事。

translations.literal: Yongyi's views on affairs clashed with Tonghe's, and he was therefore removed from the Council and also relieved of his Zongli Yamen duties.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yongyi's policy views clashed with Weng Tonghe's, he was expelled from the Grand Council and stripped of his Yamen post as well.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，皇太后再訓政，復直總署，迺密薦太常寺卿袁昶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Empress Dowager resumed personal rule; he again attended the Yamen and thereupon secretly recommended Yuan Chang, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24, after the Empress Dowager resumed rule, he returned to the Yamen and privately recommended Yuan Chang of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 會許景澄奉使還，被命同入署。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Jingcheng returned from a diplomatic mission and was ordered to enter the Yamen together with him.
translations.idiomatic: About then Xu Jingcheng came back from abroad and was ordered to join the Yamen with him.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳禍起。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer calamity arose.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 26 the Boxer disaster broke out.

sentences.zh: 先是上以行新政為中外所推，而儲嗣久虛。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had been praised at home and abroad for carrying out new policies, yet the heir had long remained unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had lately won praise at home and abroad for reform, but the succession had stood vacant for years.

sentences.zh: 載漪既用事，陰謀廢立，慮外人為梗，聞拳民有神勇，仇西教，欲倚以集事，召入京，遂縱恣不可制。

translations.literal: Once Zaiyi held power he plotted in secret to depose and enthrone, fearing foreigners would obstruct him; hearing that Boxers had divine valor and hated Western religion, he wished to rely on them to accomplish his design, summoned them to the capital, and they then ran riot beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zaiyi was in charge he plotted deposition and enthronement in secret, fearing foreign interference; told the Boxers were supernaturally brave and hated Christianity, he meant to use them to carry out his plan, called them to Beijing, and they soon could not be restrained.

sentences.zh: 用儀請嚴禁遏，不聽。

translations.literal: Yongyi requested strict prohibition and suppression, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyi urged stern prohibition and suppression, but no one listened.

sentences.zh: 俄戕德使克林德，用儀駭曰：「禍始此矣！」

translations.literal: Before long the German minister Klemens von Ketteler was killed; Yongyi said in alarm: "Disaster begins here!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon the German minister von Ketteler was murdered; Yongyi cried in alarm, "The calamity starts here!"

sentences.zh: 言於慶親王奕劻，厚歛之。

translations.literal: He spoke to Prince Qing Yikuang, who collected funds in large amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He told Prince Qing Yikuang, who raised a heavy sum of money.

sentences.zh: 各國兵艦至津沽，詔廷臣集議和戰。

translations.literal: Warships of the various powers reached Taku; an edict ordered court ministers to assemble and debate peace and war.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign warships reached Taku; the throne ordered ministers to meet and debate war or peace.

sentences.zh: 用儀、景澄、昶及尚書立山、內閣學士聯元並言：「奸民不可縱，外为不可啟。」

translations.literal: Yongyi, Jingcheng, Chang, and Minister Li Shan and Hanlin Bachelor Lian Yuan all said together: "Wicked commoners must not be indulged; foreign trouble must not be provoked."
translations.idiomatic: Yongyi, Jingcheng, Chang, Minister Li Shan, and Hanlin Bachelor Lian Yuan jointly declared, "Riotous mobs must not be indulged, and foreign conflict must not be started."

sentences.zh: 而載漪等主戰甚力，在廷大臣率依違不決。

translations.literal: Yet Zaiyi and others pressed for war with great force, and ministers at court mostly wavered and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: But Zaiyi and his party argued fiercely for war, and most ministers at court vacillated without a decision.

sentences.zh: 用儀以太后命詣使館議緩兵，當事者益目為奸邪。

translations.literal: Yongyi, on the Empress Dowager's order, went to the legations to negotiate a truce; those in charge regarded him all the more as a traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Sent by the Empress Dowager to the legations to negotiate a pause in fighting, Yongyi was seen by the war party as all the more treacherous.

sentences.zh: 景澄、昶先被害，用儀知不免，意氣自如。

translations.literal: Jingcheng and Chang were killed first; Yongyi knew he could not escape yet remained composed in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Jingcheng and Chang were executed first; Yongyi knew his end was near yet kept his bearing calm.

sentences.zh: 七月既望，遽發拳匪捕之於家，擁至莊王邸。

translations.literal: On the full moon of the seventh month Boxers suddenly seized him at his home and escorted him to Prince Zhuang's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month Boxers suddenly arrested him at home and marched him to Prince Zhuang's residence.

sentences.zh: 用儀不置辯，第曰：「天降奇禍，死固分耳！」

translations.literal: Yongyi offered no defense and only said: "Heaven sends this strange calamity; death is my allotted share!"
translations.idiomatic: Yongyi made no defense and only said, "Heaven has sent this extraordinary disaster; to die is only my due!"

sentences.zh: 遂與立山、聯元同棄市。

translations.literal: He was then executed in the marketplace together with Li Shan and Lian Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then publicly executed together with Li Shan and Lian Yuan.

sentences.zh: 越三日，聯軍入京，而兩宮西狩。

translations.literal: Three days later the allied armies entered the capital while the two sovereigns fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the allied forces entered Beijing as the two courts fled west.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔湔雪，復故官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict cleared their names and restored their former offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict rehabilitated them and restored their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，追諡忠愍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was posthumously given the title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 he received the posthumous title Zhongmin, Loyal and Suffering.

sentences.zh: 浙人祠之西湖，與景澄、昶並稱「三忠」。

translations.literal: Men of Zhejiang enshrined him at West Lake; together with Jingcheng and Chang they were called the "Three Loyal Ones."
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang gentry built him a shrine at West Lake; with Jingcheng and Chang he was known as one of the "Three Loyal Ones."

sentences.zh: 許景澄，字竹篔，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Xu Jingcheng, courtesy name Zhuyun, was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingcheng, whose courtesy name was Zhuyun, came from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed an editor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 7 he became a metropolitan graduate, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was made an editor.

sentences.zh: 明習時事，大學士文祥以使才薦。

translations.literal: He was well versed in current affairs; Grand Secretary Wenshang recommended him for diplomatic talent.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in current affairs, he was recommended by Grand Secretary Wenshang for talent in foreign service.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，詔使日本，遭父憂，未行。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was ordered to serve as envoy to Japan but met his father's death and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 6 he was ordered envoy to Japan, but his father died and he never went.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補侍講。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made a supervising reader.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed supervising reader.

sentences.zh: 法越之役，條上籌備事宜，上褒納。

translations.literal: During the Sino-French War he submitted in detail plans for preparedness; the Emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sino-French War he laid out preparedness measures in a memorial, which the throne praised and adopted.

sentences.zh: 十年，出使法德意和奧五國大臣，兼攝比國使務。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as minister to France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, and Austria, and concurrently handled Belgian affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he became minister to France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, and Austria, and concurrently to Belgium.

sentences.zh: 時海軍初創，從德國購造鐵艦，未就。

translations.literal: At that time the navy was newly founded; ironclads were being purchased from Germany but were not yet completed.
translations.idiomatic: The navy had just been created; ironclads ordered from Germany were still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 景澄躬歷船廠，鉤稽輯上外國師船表。

translations.literal: Jingcheng personally visited the shipyards, investigated and compiled, and submitted a table of foreign warships and instructors.
translations.idiomatic: Jingcheng inspected the yards himself, verified the figures, and submitted a register of foreign warships and instructors.

sentences.zh: 又言海軍宜定屯埠膠州灣，設鐵甲尓船大沽口。

translations.literal: He also said the navy ought to fix its base at Jiaozhou Bay and station ironclads at the Dagu mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged fixing the fleet's base at Jiaozhou Bay and posting ironclads at Dagu.

sentences.zh: 轉侍讀，母憂歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to reader-in-waiting and returned home on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Made reader-in-waiting, he then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 十六年，充出使俄德奧和四國大臣，累遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he served as minister to Russia, Germany, Austria, and the Netherlands, and was promoted in succession to Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he became minister to Russia, Germany, Austria, and the Netherlands, rising in time to Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 先是俄兵游獵，常越界，侵及帕米爾地，景澄爭之，俄援舊議定界起烏什別里山，自此而南屬中國，其西南屬俄。

translations.literal: Earlier Russian soldiers on hunting expeditions often crossed the border and encroached on the Pamirs; Jingcheng disputed this; Russia cited the old agreement that the boundary began at Wushibieli Mountain, from which southward belonged to China and southwestward to Russia.
translations.idiomatic: Russian troops hunting beyond the border had long encroached on the Pamirs; Jingcheng contested this, while Russia invoked the old treaty line from Mount Wushibieli south to China and southwest to Russia.

sentences.zh: 俄人則欲以薩雷闊勒為界。

translations.literal: The Russians wished to take the Sarikol Pass as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Russia wanted the Sarikol Pass as the border.

sentences.zh: 相持三載，俄始允改議，其帕界未定以前，各不進兵，以保和好。

translations.literal: The dispute lasted three years before Russia agreed to revise the talks; until the Pamir boundary was fixed neither side would advance troops, to preserve amity.
translations.idiomatic: After three years Russia agreed to reopen talks; until the Pamir line was settled neither side would move troops, to keep the peace.

sentences.zh: 因著帕米爾圖說、西北邊界地名考證，為他日界約備。

translations.literal: He therefore wrote An Illustrated Account of the Pamirs and Textual Verification of Northwestern Border Place-Names, as preparation for a future boundary treaty.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote An Illustrated Account of the Pamirs and Textual Verification of Northwestern Border Place-Names to prepare a future boundary agreement.

sentences.zh: 擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 是時俄、德迫日人還遼東，景澄曰：「俄謀自便，德圖償報，事故從此多矣！」

translations.literal: At that time Russia and Germany pressed Japan to return Liaodong; Jingcheng said: "Russia plots for its own convenience, Germany seeks repayment; troubles will multiply from this!"
translations.idiomatic: When Russia and Germany forced Japan to return Liaodong, Jingcheng warned, "Russia schemes for itself and Germany for compensation—trouble will multiply from this!"

sentences.zh: 疏請分遣兩使，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting two envoys be sent separately, and the request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to send two separate envoys, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，調充德國使臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to serve as minister to Germany.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he was reassigned as minister to Germany.

sentences.zh: 會俄建西比利亞鐵道，謀自黑龍江達海參崴，朝議拒之，迺更名商辦，許中國投貲五百萬，所謂東清鐵路公司也。

translations.literal: At that time Russia was building the Siberian railway, planning to reach Vladivostok from the Amur; the court debated refusal; it was then renamed a commercial venture, and China was allowed to invest five million taels—the so-called Chinese Eastern Railway Company.
translations.idiomatic: Russia was building the Siberian line toward Vladivostok from the Amur; after court debate the project was recast as a joint commercial railway with five million taels of Chinese capital—the Chinese Eastern Railway Company.

sentences.zh: 詔景澄綜其事，力阻路悋南溢，稽察運船毋漏稅。

translations.literal: Jingcheng was ordered to oversee the matter, strenuously blocking the line's rights from spilling southward and auditing transport ships so taxes would not be evaded.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to oversee the railway, he fought to keep its rights from spreading south and audited shipping so duties were not evaded.

sentences.zh: 已而俄人索租旅順，充頭等公使，會駐俄使臣楊儒定議俄都。

translations.literal: Before long the Russians demanded lease of Port Arthur; he served as first-class minister and joined the resident envoy Yang Ru in negotiating at the Russian capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Russia demanded Port Arthur on lease; as first-class minister he joined envoy Yang Ru in talks at St. Petersburg.

sentences.zh: 事竣，移疾歸，召授總理各國事務大臣兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the business was finished he resigned on grounds of illness and returned; he was summoned and appointed Zongli Yamen minister and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When negotiations ended he returned on sick leave, then was recalled as Zongli Yamen minister and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 調吏部，充大學堂總教習、管學大臣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Personnel and served as chief instructor and superintendent of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Personnel, he became chief instructor and superintendent of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 意大利索我三門灣，景澄抗言爭之，事迺寢。

translations.literal: Italy demanded our Sanmen Bay; Jingcheng resisted and argued; the matter then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When Italy demanded Sanmen Bay, Jingcheng argued back until the claim was dropped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拳禍作，景澄召見時，歷陳兵为不可啟，春秋之義，不殺行人，圍攻使館，實背公法。

translations.literal: Before long the Boxer calamity broke out; when Jingcheng was summoned for audience he set forth in detail that military trouble must not be started, that the Spring and Autumn principle forbids killing envoys, and that besieging legations truly violated public law.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer crisis erupted and Jingcheng was summoned, he insisted war must not be started, cited the Spring and Autumn rule against killing envoys, and said besieging legations violated international law.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之動容，而載漪等斥為邪說。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was moved on hearing this, but Zaiyi and others denounced it as heterodox doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was visibly moved, but Zaiyi and his party called it pernicious talk.

sentences.zh: 聯軍偪近畿，景澄等遂坐主和棄市。

translations.literal: When the allied armies pressed close to the capital, Jingcheng and others were executed on the charge of favoring peace.
translations.idiomatic: As the allies neared the capital, Jingcheng and others were executed for advocating peace.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，追諡文肅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was posthumously given the title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 he received the posthumous title Wensu, Cultured and Stern.

sentences.zh: 袁昶，字爽秋，桐廬人。

translations.literal: Yuan Chang, courtesy name Shuangqiu, was a native of Tonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chang, whose courtesy name was Shuangqiu, came from Tonglu.

sentences.zh: 從劉熙載讀，博通掌故。

translations.literal: He studied under Liu Xizai and was broadly versed in historical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Xizai and mastered institutional history.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，授戶部主事，充總理各國事務衙門章京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and served as a Zongli Yamen clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 2 he became a metropolitan graduate, entered Revenue as principal secretary, and served as a Yamen clerk.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以員外郎出任徽寧池太廣道。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, as an assistant department director, he went out to serve as intendant of the Huaining-Chizhou-Taiping-Guangde circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he left the capital as intendant of the Huaining-Chizhou-Taiping-Guangde circuit.

sentences.zh: 誡僚屬，抑胥吏，多所興革；

translations.literal: He admonished subordinates, restrained clerks, and carried out many reforms;
translations.idiomatic: He warned his staff, reined in clerks, and instituted many reforms;

sentences.zh: 擴中江書院齋舍，課以實學；

translations.literal: he expanded the dormitories of the Zhongjiang Academy and taught practical learning;
translations.idiomatic: he enlarged Zhongjiang Academy quarters and taught practical learning;

sentences.zh: 建尊經閣，購書數萬卷；

translations.literal: he built the Hall for Honoring the Classics and purchased tens of thousands of volumes;
translations.idiomatic: he built a Hall for Honoring the Classics and bought tens of thousands of books;

sentences.zh: 汰常關耗費歲萬八千金，悉還諸公；

translations.literal: he eliminated eighteen thousand taels of yearly waste at the regular customs post and returned it all to the public account;
translations.idiomatic: he cut eighteen thousand taels of yearly waste at the regular customs house and returned it to the public purse;

sentences.zh: 定專條，納新關穀米出口稅，歲羨數十萬；

translations.literal: he fixed special regulations, collected export tax on grain at the new customs post, and yearly surplus ran to several hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: he set special rules for grain export tax at the new customs house, yielding hundreds of thousands in surplus each year;

sentences.zh: 督修蕪湖西南濱江圩隄，自大關亭至魯港，延袤十二里；

translations.literal: he supervised repair of the river embankment along the southwest bank at Wuhu, from Daguan Pavilion to Lugang, extending twelve li;
translations.idiomatic: he oversaw repairs to Wuhu's southwest river embankment from Daguan Pavilion to Lugang, twelve li in length;

sentences.zh: 更穿築新縷隄三百七十丈，自是蓄洩有資，田廬完固，民歌誦之。

translations.literal: he further dug and built a new continuous embankment three hundred seventy zhang long; thereafter storage and drainage had support, fields and houses were secure, and the people sang his praise.
translations.idiomatic: he added a new continuous dike three hundred seventy zhang long; flooding could then be controlled, farms and homes were safe, and the people praised him in song.

sentences.zh: 膠州事起，下詔求言，昶條列時政二萬餘言，以：「德突據膠灣，其禍急而小；

translations.literal: When the Jiaozhou affair arose the throne called for memorials; Chang set forth more than twenty thousand characters on current policy, saying: "Germany's sudden seizure of Jiaozhou is a calamity urgent yet small;
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiaozhou crisis the throne sought advice; Chang submitted more than twenty thousand characters, arguing Germany's seizure of Jiaozhou was urgent but small,

sentences.zh: 俄自西北至東北，與我壤地相錯，蒙喀四十八部將折入異域，其禍紆而大。

translations.literal: Russia from the northwest to the northeast shares intertwined territory with us; the forty-eight Mongol and Khalkha banners will be folded into foreign lands—the calamity is winding yet great.
translations.idiomatic: while Russia's reach from northwest to northeast entangles our soil and threatens forty-eight Mongol and Khalkha banners with absorption—a slower, greater peril.

sentences.zh: 宜及今預練勁旅，痛革吉、奉華靡風習。

translations.literal: We ought even now to train crack troops beforehand and thoroughly reform the extravagant habits of Jilin and Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He urged training elite troops now and rooting out the luxurious habits of Jilin and Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 自頃兵力不能議戰，要不可不議守。

translations.literal: Lately our military strength cannot sustain debate on war, yet we absolutely cannot fail to debate defense.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces could not yet sustain war, he said, but defense could not be neglected.

sentences.zh: 我朝八旗初制，文武不分途，京外不分途，人皆兵，官皆將，故人才盛，國勢強。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's original Eight Banner system made no distinction between civil and military tracks, nor between capital and provinces; every man was a soldier and every official a general; therefore talent flourished and national strength was great.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original Eight Banner system civil and military, capital and province were one; every man was a soldier and every officer a commander, so talent abounded and the state was strong.

sentences.zh: 承平日久，文法繁密，諸臣救過之不暇，於是相率為鄉愿，而舉國之人才靡矣！

translations.literal: After long peace the code grew intricate; ministers had no leisure beyond correcting faults; they therefore followed one another in timid conformity, and the nation's talent withered!
translations.idiomatic: Long peace bred intricate regulations; officials scrambled only to avoid blame, fell into timid conformity, and national talent withered.

sentences.zh: 金田洪、楊之亂，其始一小民耳，猶窮全國之力僅而克之，況諸國互肆蠶食之心，有不乘吾敝而攻吾之短者哉？

translations.literal: The Hong and Yang rebellion of Jintian began with a single commoner, yet the empire's full strength barely overcame it; how much more when many states all harbor designs of nibbling us—will there not be those who seize our weakness and strike our flaws?
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping revolt began with ordinary villagers yet nearly exhausted the empire; with many powers eager to devour us, who would not strike when we were weak?

sentences.zh: 夫敵國外患，為殷憂啟聖之資。

translations.literal: Foreign enemies and external troubles are resources by which deep anxiety awakens sagely rule.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign foes and external peril, he wrote, are what awaken sagely rule through grave anxiety.

sentences.zh: 苟得其人，毋拘以文法，則理財、練兵、防海、交鄰之策，可次第就理。」

translations.literal: If the right men are obtained and not bound by written regulations, then policies for finance, training troops, coastal defense, and foreign relations can be set in order step by step."
translations.idiomatic: Given the right men, unbound by red tape, finance, armies, coast defense, and diplomacy could be put in order one by one."

sentences.zh: 上親書其綱要於冊，下中外大臣議行。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally copied its main points into a booklet and sent it down to Chinese and foreign ministers for discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor copied its main points into a booklet and circulated them to ministers at home and abroad for action.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷陝西按察使，未到官，擢江寧布政使，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Shaanxi judicial commissioner; before taking office he was promoted to Jiangning financial commissioner and transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he was named Shaanxi judicial commissioner, then promoted to Jiangning financial commissioner and moved to Zhili before taking the first post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，內召，以三品京堂在總理衙門行走，授光祿寺卿，轉太常寺卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the capital; as a third-rank capital official he served at the Zongli Yamen, was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon recalled to Beijing, he served at the Yamen as a third-rank capital official, became Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時財用匱，議整釐稅。

translations.literal: At that time finances were depleted and there was debate on reorganizing the likin tax.
translations.idiomatic: Finances were depleted and officials debated reorganizing the likin tax.

sentences.zh: 昶極言釐金名病商，實病民，不可議增。

translations.literal: Chang strongly argued that likin by name harms merchants but in fact harms the people, and must not be increased.
translations.idiomatic: Chang insisted likin nominally hurt merchants but really hurt the people and must not be raised.

sentences.zh: 義和團起山東，屠戮外國教士。

translations.literal: The Boxers arose in Shandong and slaughtered foreign missionaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Boxer movement rose in Shandong and massacred foreign missionaries.

sentences.zh: 昶與許景澄相善，廷詢時，陳奏皆谒慨，上執景澄手而泣。

translations.literal: Chang was on good terms with Xu Jingcheng; when questioned at court their statements were all forthright; the Emperor grasped Jingcheng's hand and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Close to Xu Jingcheng, Chang spoke as bluntly as he at court audiences; the emperor took Jingcheng's hand and wept.

sentences.zh: 昶連上二疏，力言奸民不可縱，使臣不宜殺，皆不報。

translations.literal: Chang submitted two memorials in succession, strongly stating that wicked commoners must not be indulged and envoys must not be killed; none received response.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent two memorials in succession urging that rioters not be indulged and envoys not be killed; neither was answered.

sentences.zh: 復與景澄合上第三疏，嚴劾釀亂大臣，未及奏，已被禍，疏稿為世稱誦。

translations.literal: He again joined Jingcheng in submitting a third memorial, sternly impeaching the ministers who brewed the disorder; before it could be presented he had already met disaster; the draft was praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jingcheng drafted a third memorial impeaching the ministers who brewed the crisis; before it reached the throne he was dead, yet the draft became famous.

sentences.zh: 追諡忠節，江南人祠之蕪湖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Zhongjie; people of Jiangnan enshrined him at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously titled Zhongjie, Loyal and Upright, he was enshrined at Wuhu by Jiangnan gentry.

sentences.zh: 昶嘗慨士鮮實學，輯農桑、兵、醫、輿地、治術、掌故諸書，為漸西村叢刻。

translations.literal: Chang once lamented that scholars lacked practical learning and compiled books on agriculture, sericulture, military affairs, medicine, geography, statecraft, and institutional precedent into the Jianxi Village Collectanea.
translations.idiomatic: Lamenting scholars' lack of practical learning, he compiled works on farming, sericulture, war, medicine, geography, statecraft, and precedent as the Jianxi Village Collectanea.

sentences.zh: 立山，字豫甫，土默特氏，蒙古正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Li Shan, courtesy name Yufu, of the Tumet clan, was a Mongol of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shan, courtesy name Yufu, of the Tumet clan, was a Mongol of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，以員外郎出監蘇州織造，歷四任迺得代。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, as an assistant department director, he went out to supervise Suzhou weaving and served four terms before he could be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 5 he went out as assistant director to supervise Suzhou weaving and held the post four terms before relief.

sentences.zh: 論修南苑工，賜二品服。

translations.literal: For discussing repairs to the Southern Park works he was granted second-rank court dress.
translations.idiomatic: For supervising Southern Park repairs he was granted second-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 累遷奉宸苑卿、總管內務府大臣、正白旗漢軍副都統、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Director of the Imperial Parks, Superintendent of the Imperial Household, Vice Commander of the Plain White Banner Chinese Brigade, and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through director of imperial parks, household superintendent, vice commander of the Plain White Chinese Banner, to vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he received the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 盜竊寧壽宮物，坐失察，鐫職留任。

translations.literal: When objects were stolen from the Ningshou Palace he was punished for failure of supervision, his rank was cut, yet he retained his post.
translations.idiomatic: After theft from Ningshou Palace he was demoted for lax supervision but kept in office.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 立山久典內廷，同列嫉其寵眷。

translations.literal: Li Shan had long managed the inner court; colleagues envied his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Long in charge of the inner court, he was envied by colleagues for imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 會拳禍起，聯軍至天津，廷臣集議御前。

translations.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose and the allied armies reached Tianjin, court ministers assembled for deliberation before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer crisis broke and allies reached Tianjin, ministers met in audience before the throne.

sentences.zh: 載漪盛推拳民可用，立山適在側，太后謂：「汝言如何？」

translations.literal: Zaiyi strongly praised the Boxers as usable; Li Shan happened to be at the side; the Empress Dowager said: "What is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi loudly insisted the Boxers could be used; Li Shan stood nearby when the Empress Dowager asked, "What do you say?"

sentences.zh: 立山曰：「拳民雖無他，然其術多不驗．」載漪怒曰：「用其心耳，奚問術？

translations.literal: Li Shan said: "Though the Boxers have no other fault, their arts mostly do not work." Zaiyi angrily said: "Use their hearts—that is all; why ask about arts?
translations.idiomatic: Li Shan replied, "The Boxers may mean well, but their magic seldom works." Zaiyi snapped, "We need their loyalty—why quibble over tricks?

sentences.zh: 立山必與外人通，請以立山退外兵！」

translations.literal: Li Shan must be in league with foreigners; I request that Li Shan be sent to drive off the foreign armies!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Shan must be colluding with foreigners—send him to make the foreign troops withdraw!"

sentences.zh: 立山曰：「首言戰者載漪也！

translations.literal: Li Shan said: "The first to speak for war was Zaiyi!
translations.idiomatic: Li Shan answered, "Zaiyi was the first to urge war!

sentences.zh: 臣主和，又不諳外事，不足任。」

translations.literal: Your servant favors peace and is moreover unskilled in foreign affairs—not fit for the task."
translations.idiomatic: I favor peace and know nothing of foreign affairs; I am not fit for the task."

sentences.zh: 載漪益仇之，因其宅讫教堂，迺中以蜚語，謂藏匿外人，竟論死。

translations.literal: Zaiyi hated him all the more; because his residence had once been a church, he was then struck by slanderous talk that he harbored foreigners, and he was finally sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi hated him more than ever; because his house had been a church, rumor said he hid foreigners, and he was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，追諡忠貞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was posthumously given the title Zhongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 he received the posthumous title Zhongzhen, Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 聯元，字仙蘅，崔佳氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Lian Yuan, courtesy name Xianheng, of the Cuijia clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Yuan, courtesy name Xianheng, of the Cuijia clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，累遷侍講。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed reviser, and was promoted in succession to supervising reader.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 7 he became a metropolitan graduate and Hanlin bachelor, was made reviser, and rose to supervising reader.

sentences.zh: 大考，左遷中允，再陟侍講。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he was demoted to junior expositor and again rose to supervising reader.
translations.idiomatic: After a poor grand examination he was demoted to junior expositor, then promoted again to supervising reader.

sentences.zh: 以京察，出知安徽太平府，調安慶。

translations.literal: Through the capital inspection he went out as prefect of Taiping in Anhui and was transferred to Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: On a capital inspection he became prefect of Taiping in Anhui, then was moved to Anqing.

sentences.zh: 兩薦卓異，署滁和道，遷廣東惠潮嘉道。

translations.literal: Twice recommended as outstanding, he acted as intendant of Chuzhou and He prefectures and was transferred to intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Twice rated outstanding, he served as acting intendant on the Chuzhou-He circuit and then as intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 汕頭者，通商要衢也，奸人倚英領事為民暴，聯元裁以法，良善獲安。

translations.literal: Shantou was a key port for foreign trade; wicked men relied on the British consul to tyrannize the people; Lian Yuan judged them by law and the good obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: At Shantou, a vital treaty port, ruffians sheltered behind the British consul to prey on the people until Lian Yuan punished them by law and the law-abiding were safe.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，擢安徽按察使，入覲，改三品京堂，在總理衙門行走。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to Anhui judicial commissioner; on entering audience he was made a third-rank capital official serving at the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24 he became Anhui judicial commissioner; after audience he was made a third-rank capital official at the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 又明年，補內閣學士。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 拳民仇西教，載漪、剛毅助之，勢益橫，日夜圍攻使館，不能下。

translations.literal: The Boxers hated Western religion; Zaiyi and Gang Yi supported them; their power grew all the more overbearing; day and night they besieged the legations but could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Boxers hated Christianity; backed by Zaiyi and Gang Yi they grew bolder, besieging the legations day and night without success.

sentences.zh: 大臣負清望者徐桐、崇綺，皆謂：「民氣可用。」

translations.literal: Ministers of high repute, Xu Tong and Chongqi, all said: "Popular spirit can be used."
translations.idiomatic: Respected ministers Xu Tong and Chongqi both declared, "The people's spirit can be harnessed."

sentences.zh: 聯元與崇綺爭論帝前，謂：「民氣可用，匪氣不可用。」

translations.literal: Lian Yuan debated with Chongqi before the Emperor, saying: "Popular spirit can be used; bandit spirit cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor Lian Yuan argued with Chongqi: "Popular spirit may be used, but bandit spirit must not."

sentences.zh: 聯軍既陷大沽，載漪等猶壹意主戰。

translations.literal: After the allied armies had taken Dagu, Zaiyi and others still single-mindedly favored war.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the allies captured Dagu, Zaiyi and his party still insisted on war.

sentences.zh: 聯元謂：「甲午之役，一日本且不能勝，況八強國乎？

translations.literal: Lian Yuan said: "In the war of Jiawu, China could not even defeat Japan alone—how much less eight great powers?
translations.idiomatic: Lian Yuan said, "In the Sino-Japanese War we could not beat Japan alone—what chance against eight great powers?

sentences.zh: 儻戰而敗，如宗廟何？」

translations.literal: If we fight and are defeated, what of the ancestral temples?"
translations.idiomatic: If we fight and lose, what becomes of the ancestral shrines?"

sentences.zh: 載漪斥其言不祥，七月十七日，斬西市。

translations.literal: Zaiyi denounced his words as ill-omened; on the seventeenth day of the seventh month he was beheaded at the West Market.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi called his words unlucky; on the seventeenth of the seventh month he was beheaded at the West Market.

sentences.zh: 昭雪後，予諡文直。

translations.literal: After rehabilitation he was given the posthumous title Wenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: After rehabilitation he received the posthumous title Wenzhi, Cultured and Upright.

sentences.zh: 順天府奏請立山、聯元合祠宣武門外，而聯元祖居寶坻，更於其地建專祠焉。

translations.literal: Shuntian prefecture memorialized requesting a joint shrine for Li Shan and Lian Yuan outside Xuanwu Gate; because Lian Yuan's ancestral home was in Baodi, a separate shrine was also built there.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian requested a joint shrine to Li Shan and Lian Yuan outside Xuanwu Gate; because Lian Yuan's family came from Baodi, a separate shrine was built there as well.

sentences.zh: 論曰：清代優禮廷臣，罕有誅罰。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Qing dynasty treated court ministers with favor and rarely punished them.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The Qing usually honored court ministers and seldom put them to death.

sentences.zh: 拳禍既起，忠諫大臣駢首就戮，豈獨非帝意哉？

translations.literal: Once the Boxer calamity arose, loyal remonstrating ministers were slaughtered in rows—was this solely contrary to the Emperor's intent?
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer crisis came, loyal ministers who spoke out were executed in batches—surely this was not the emperor's wish alone?

sentences.zh: 觀用儀諸人所論事勢利害，昭昭如此，迺終不能回當軸之聽，何其昧焉？

translations.literal: Considering the advantages and harms of the situation as Yongyi and the others discussed them, so clear as this, yet in the end they could not turn the ears of those in power—how blind?
translations.idiomatic: The case Yongyi and his fellows made for war or peace was plain enough, yet those in power would not listen—how blind were they?

sentences.zh: 世傳大節，並號「五忠」，不數日而遂昭雪，允哉！

translations.literal: The world transmits their great integrity; together they were called the "Five Loyal Ones"; within a few days they were rehabilitated—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Posterity honors their integrity as the "Five Loyal Ones"; within days they were cleared—rightly so!
